A barb-tailed imp holds court from the r: A barb-tailed imp holds court from the rafters with a hobgoblin enforcer it has bribed into the role of bodyguard. It points imperiously; the hobgoblin sighs and obliges — while the imp keeps flicking its needle of a tail across you, and where it cuts the room starts to swim.
A cell wight stands over a famished ghas: A cell wight stands over a famished ghast like a gaoler over a starved dog. One drains the strength from your arm; the other waits for the moment the strength is gone.
A crimson imp perches on the highest she: A crimson imp perches on the highest shelf, laughing as it kicks one of the cages. A chalk-grey mephit pours from the broken seal.
A famished ghast and a single goblin sha: A famished ghast and a single goblin share the same dead-end — the goblin keeping well clear of the ghast, both of them turning toward the warmer thing in the doorway.
A gaol-dog comes off its chain at a dead: A gaol-dog comes off its chain at a dead sprint — and the goblin handler who lost hold of it comes running after, too embarrassed not to finish what the dog started.
A ghoul looks up from something it has h: A ghoul looks up from something it has half-eaten, fingers still in the ribs of it. A skeleton stands at attention behind, like a butler at a long-delayed supper.
A glass jar lies cracked on the bench, c: A glass jar lies cracked on the bench, chalk-grey dust pouring out in the shape of a mephit. It opens its eyes as you cross the threshold.
A goblin scout draws a chipped blade and: A goblin scout draws a chipped blade and grins all the way to its ears — and the rafters above shift at the same moment, a stirge dropping out of the dark with its proboscis already open.
A goblin warden in scavenged half-plate: A goblin warden in scavenged half-plate has stationed himself at the corridor turn with a hobgoblin sergeant at his shoulder. Neither speaks. The warden's bell rings once. The sergeant moves.

A goblin warden in scavenged half-plate leans on the pulley as if he owns the corridor. A stirge drops from the rafters at the sound of your boots, looking for whatever the warden has been bleeding for sport.
A goblin warden of higher trim than the: A goblin warden of higher trim than the corridor scouts stands at the doorway with a goblin grunt at each elbow. He has been bored. He looks pleased now.
A gray-dwarf overseer leans on a two-han: A gray-dwarf overseer leans on a two-handed maul at the foot of the stair, in no hurry at all. He has run this block thirty years on one principle: there is always another goblin in the dark, and always work to break it on. He whistles down the stair to prove it.
A hobgoblin drillmaster in shined half-p: A hobgoblin drillmaster in shined half-plate stands at parade-rest. A goblin recruit cowers behind it — until the drillmaster's flat command-voice lands on you both at once: the goblin remembers what it's for, and some trained-in part of your own arm flinches before you can stop it.
A pair of kobolds bicker over the corpse: A pair of kobolds bicker over the corpse of something soft. They stop bickering when they see you.
A plague-bred gaol-dog pads the corridor: A plague-bred gaol-dog pads the corridor with a kobold handler who has long since stopped holding the chain. Both are overdue for something to bite.
A prisoner died in this cell with the ma: A prisoner died in this cell with the manacle still on, and got up wearing it. The iron has fused into the wrist-bone. It reaches for you with the other hand.
A side-chamber reeks of damp fur and old: A side-chamber reeks of damp fur and old blood. A hulking goblinoid crouches over a pile of coin and other men's teeth. It hefts a spiked maul and grunts a challenge — bored, until you make it bleed, and then it hauls the maul up overhead and stops being bored at all.
A side-passage with a broken lantern. Th: A side-passage with a broken lantern. The walls are scratched with prayers in a language you almost know.
A skeleton drags itself upright over the: A skeleton drags itself upright over the bones of an older one. The older one is also still moving — slower, patient. They were buried as a pair.
A skeleton stands over a heap of older b: A skeleton stands over a heap of older bones, a stirge fattening on what little blood is left. Both turn in unison.
A starved ghast crouches over a stripped: A starved ghast crouches over a stripped ribcage, too far gone to stalk. It hears you, and the patience leaves it all at once.
A stretch of stair the ceiling came down: A stretch of stair the ceiling came down on, sealing the corridor behind you. For a little while, at least, nothing can follow.
A trembling prisoner the slavers kept as: A trembling prisoner the slavers kept as a quartermaster has a stash behind a loose stone — arms stripped from the dead, draughts skimmed from the labs. He wants coin, not company.
An altar of weathered stone, three sigil: An altar of weathered stone, three sigils flickering as you approach. The labs above never sealed this off — gods bleed through cracks the master cannot find.
An empty harness stands sentinel in the: An empty harness stands sentinel in the next chamber. The plates ring like a bell as it pivots to face you — a faint green light moves where the eyes should be.
Bone clatters on stone — and then again,: Bone clatters on stone — and then again, a heartbeat later. Two heaps of armor scraps rise at once. Whatever the master kept down here, he forgot to bury this pair twice.
The bugbear is back, or another of his c: The bugbear is back, or another of his cousins — and this one keeps something on a length of rusted chain. A ghoul, drooling, eyes mad with the patience of a thing that has been kept hungry on purpose.
The duergar slaver waits at the centre o: The duergar slaver waits at the centre of a wide stone hall. He spits on the floor when he sees you. "Another of his pets, are you? Walking. Tch. We'll see how long."
The largest jar on the bench has gone th: The largest jar on the bench has gone the colour of old ledger paper from the inside, and the lid is sitting on the floor beside it. Something three times the size of the others is uncoiling out.
The rafters above are thick with shapes. One drops first, proboscis open for whoever stands in the lantern light — a kobold below draws a blade, less from courage than from not wanting to share its meal.
The vault doubles as a tomb, and the tom: The vault doubles as a tomb, and the tomb doubles as a larder. An animated armor strides between two ghouls feeding in the corner. The plates ring once. The ghouls turn.
Three days south of the Iron Cells the t: Three days south of the Iron Cells the trees thin, and the Trade Way bends towards Amn. A caravan-merchant has a fire going by the milestone — kettle on, ox unhitched, a tarp pegged out in case the night turns. He looks up without surprise, as if he had been expecting someone walking out of the north on foot and bloody.
Two kobolds skitter at the edge of the l: Two kobolds skitter at the edge of the lantern light. Smaller than you, and meaner in pairs — they have already agreed who comes from which angle.
Two pairs of yellow eyes — a goblin and: Two pairs of yellow eyes — a goblin and a smaller kobold conscript backing it. They split as they come, hoping you only see one.
Two paupers were buried together in this: Two paupers were buried together in this hole and one of them has gotten back up wearing the other, the hanging-chain still knotted around its wrist. A skeleton stands beside it, less ambitious — content with its own bones — while the wight reaches for you with a hand gone grave-cold, to hold you still for the rest.
Two stirges drop from the rafters in suc: Two stirges drop from the rafters in succession, the second a heartbeat behind the first — close enough that you cannot put steel to both without letting one feed.
